assessment_summary: The statement claims that every tournament on 4 vertices contains a Hamiltonian cycle. This is false. A transitive tournament on 4 vertices contains no cycles at all. For example, if we label the vertices 1, 2, 3, 4 and direct all edges from i to j whenever i < j, vertex 4 will have an out-degree of 0 (it is a sink) and vertex 1 will have an in-degree of 0 (it is a source). Since a Hamiltonian cycle must enter and leave every vertex, this tournament cannot contain a Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: Let T be a tournament on vertices V = {1, 2, 3, 4} with arcs A = {(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)}. This is a valid tournament because every pair of distinct vertices has exactly one directed edge between them. In this tournament, vertex 4 has an out-degree of 0 (there are no arcs originating from 4). Since a Hamiltonian cycle must visit every vertex and leave it to go to the next vertex, vertex 4 cannot be part of any cycle. Therefore, T has no Hamiltonian cycle.
